messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High error rate and RDMA retransmits detected on prod-gpu-2 cluster. Severity: P1. Auto-escalating to oncall and infra.
maya: hit this just now — frontend got 502 spikes, some container restarts seen. Seeing CUDA driver errors in kube logs.
sam: on it, pulling logs from pod serving-replica-47. `kubectl logs -n prod serving-replica-47 --previous` shows repeated OOM+`killed` entries.
zach: also seeing massive IB retransmit counts on nodes 12-14: `rdma_stat` shows TX retransmits increasing. Possible packet reordering causing KV cache thrash across the serving group.
oncall: taking pager. I'll gather high-level impact and coordinate mitigations. @cs-rep please collect customer-impact signals (errors, error-rate by org).
cs-rep: Customer telemetry: 12 customers reported increased latencies, 3 reported request failures in the last 15m. Top affected tenant: chat-saas-prod. We'll mark incident notices if it persists.
maya: stack traces include ``CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`` and then container restarts. Metric graph: token latency p95 jumped from 220ms -> 1.8s.
sam: running `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -i 0` on node12 shows memory oscillating before crash. Might be retry storms + KV cache growth.
infra-bot: automated network probe: ib0 interface on node12 reports frequent `link up/down` events and ECN counters spiking.
zach: putting a quick probe command here: ```sh
for n in node12 node13 node14; do ssh $n "ibdevinfo -l; cat /sys/class/net/ib0/statistics/tx_retransmit; ethtool -S ib0 | grep ecn"; done
```
oncall: good. While we collect root cause, mitigation plan options: 1) scale down distributed serving to single-node fallback (reduces performance) 2) failover traffic to dedicated capacity zone 3) cordon affected nodes + restart serving pool 4) enable TCP fallback for RDMA if supported. Thoughts?
maya: immediate short-term: cordon node12-14 to stop cross-node KV cache syncs and drain pods. That should reduce inter-node RDMA chatter. I'll coordinate draining.
sam: agree, cordon+drain. Also we should flip routing policy to route new traffic to dedicated pool `prod-dedicated-1` to protect SLAs for high-value tenants.
oncall: action item: maya cordon nodes, sam update routing, zach watch infra metrics and run `ibdiagnet` to capture traces. I'll update incident dashboard.
maya: cordoned node12-14, starting `kubectl drain node12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` now. Will mark pods as evicted. ETA ~2m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sam: updated router rules to send 80% of new requests to prod-dedicated-1, 20% to leftover hosts for graceful drain. :white_check_mark:
zach: running `ibdiagnet -w 60` on node12 to capture fabric anomalies. Early capture shows output: "reordering events: 1.2e5, retransmits: 9.8e4, ecn-marked: 7.6e4" — that's huge.
maya: draining completed for node12. Pod restarts dropped for that node. But node13 still shows restarts. Continuing.
oncall: customer impact update: error rate for chat-saas-prod reduced from 14% -> 6% after partial drain + routing change. Still degraded for a subset of sessions.
pagerduty-bot: incident acknowledged by oncall. Handoff scheduled in 35m.
sam: logs from restarted containers contain this recurring snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T02:45:12Z] runtime error: cuda: driver shutdown during kernel launch (err=700). oom_hint=1
[2026-03-15T02:45:13Z] containerd: oom_kill process pid=20388 name=llm_worker
```
zach: that maps to hardware-level packet loss causing excessive retries — flows get re-ordered, KV cache fails and memory grows due to resends. I'm going to coordinate with networking team to validate switch counters and reroute IB fabric paths.
kelly: I'm paging network infra on-call (cc: @net-oncall). Noted that ECN marking rate correlates with a maintenance window earlier in the region. Could be a bad route or mis-configured QoS.
net-oncall (via DM): acknowledged, checking TOR and spine counters. Early sign: a misprogrammed QoS queue on spine-3 causing bursts to be ECN-marked and queueing to escalate into packet reorders.
oncall: next steps summary pinned: 1) net-oncall to fix QoS rule / reroute spine 2) infra to keep cordoned nodes drained for 30m 3) sam to keep traffic split to dedicated pool 4) SRE to capture post-fix performance and KV cache metrics 5) cs to prepare customer comms if SLA affected.
maya: we also applied a temporary mitigation in serving runtime: disabled cross-node KV cache synchronization (force local-only caching) to limit thrash. Config change applied via ConfigMap rollout: ```yaml
serving.kv_cache.sync: false
serving.batch.window_ms: 8
``` Applied to prod via kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving -> starting rollout.
sam: noticed that disabling sync reduces memory growth and OOMs at the cost of slight increase in token duplication for some sessions. Acceptable for immediate mitigation.
net-oncall: network change completed — QoS rule reverted and spine-3 rerouted. Observed ECN counters drop by 95% within 90s.
zach: fabric retransmits dropping now. `rdma_stat` shows retransmit curve flattening. Good sign.
oncall: monitoring — please watch error rate and latencies for next 20m. If stable, we'll uncordon nodes gradually.
maya: rolling uncordon of node12 (already), will wait 10m then node13.
cs-rep: customer impact update: affected tenants now at 1-2% errors; chat-saas-prod reporting acceptable degraded performance, no ticket storm. I'll prepare a short status note if we reach stable.
maya: uncordoned node13 at +12m — no immediate OOMs. Reintegrating into serving pool.
sam: routing traffic back: shifting 90% back to prod pool over 5m.
oncall: post-mortem notes so far: probable chain — QoS misconfig on spine -> ECN spikes -> packet reordering -> RDMA retransmits -> KV cache thrash across nodes -> memory growth in serving runtime -> OOMs and container restarts -> frontend 5xx.
kelly: remediation checklist: 1) net team fix QoS, 2) infra add IB fabric alerts for reordering/retransmit thresholds, 3) runtime: add circuit breaker to disable cross-node sync when retransmit > threshold, 4) ops: run catastrophe drills for RDMA fabric events.
zach: collected traces and uploaded to /incidents/2174503210/artifacts/rdma_trace_node12.pcap. (link)
oncall: closing timeline: major degradations resolved by routing/draindown + net fix. We'll keep incident open for 4 hours for monitoring and follow-up. Thanks all — paging summary to follow. :tada:
